item.description: Apurinic/apyrimidinic (AP) sites are abundant but normally short-lived intermediates of base excision repair because they are rapidly processed by AP endonuclease 1 (APE1). Here, we identify benzoquinoplatin (BQP), a benzoquinoline complex with a monofunctional platinum(II) moiety, as an AP-site-directed adduct-former that covalently traps DNA lesions. item.description: Ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) has been reported to alter the expression of hepatic transporters, such as organic anion-transporting polypeptides (OATPs), and multidrug resistance-associated proteins (MRPs). item.description: BCL-X(L), an anti-apoptotic member of the BCL-2 protein family, is an attractive therapeutic target for overcoming apoptosis resistance in cancer. However, the large, shallow, and predominantly hydrophobic nature of its BH3-binding groove has complicated the discovery of potent, drug-like small-molecule inhibitors. Here, we employed structure-based virtual screening with key interaction constraints to identify novel BCL-X(L) inhibitor scaffolds with relatively low molecular weights (MWs)....

item.description: Nanoscale processing enhances the photocatalytic reactivity of titanium dioxide nanoparticles (TiO(2) NPs) under UV exposure. item.title: Unveiling the Creep Recovery Behavior of Pseudo-Free-Standing Polymer Thin Films for Wearable Electronics
item.description: Polymer thin films in wearable electronics undergo creep recovery during operation as on-body devices, resulting in unrecoverable strain that subsequently induces mechanical instability in the films. However, the creep recovery behavior of polymer thin films has not been investigated due to their intrinsic fragility and the difficulty in controlling ultralow loads for the films. We evaluate the creep recovery behavior of pseudo-free-standing polymer thin films as a function of creep stress,...

item.title: Nonlinear dose-response relationship between cumulative anticholinergic use and the risk of dementia in adults with overactive bladder: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: Dementia risk in OAB patients follows a non-linear trajectory, with a critical vulnerability window during the first 3 years of cumulative ACH exposure. Clinical management should prioritise non-anticholinergic alternatives (e.g. mirabegron) or implement structured cognitive surveillance during this early treatment phase.

item.description: Phytolacca americana L. (Phytolaccaceae), a perennial species native to North America, is rich in oleanane-type triterpenoid saponins. item.description: BACKGROUND AND AIM: Otsu-Ji-To (OJT), also known as Eul-ja-tang in Korean, is a traditional herbal formula used to treat hemorrhoids. We investigated its antiviral effects against HCoV-OC43, SARS-CoV-2, and its variants.

item.title: Integrated computational screening and biochemical validation identify natural small molecules targeting Aβ aggregation and dissociation
item.description: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by the accumulation of amyloid-β (Aβ), a pathological hallmark implicated in disease onset and progression. Aβ undergoes self-assembly from monomers into soluble oligomers, protofibrils, insoluble fibrils, and extracellular plaques. Our previous studies have shown that Jowiseungchungtang, which consists of 14 medicinal herbs, inhibits Aβ aggregation and ameliorates Aβ-mediated pathology in AD models. item.title: Spatial and Seasonal Structuring of Bacterial Communities and Putative Pathogen-Associated Bacterial Taxa at Four Korean Coastal Locations
item.description: Coastal marine environments are dynamic transition zones where offshore water masses and terrestrial inputs shape microbial community structure. However, standardized comparisons of bacterial communities across geographically distinct Korean coastal waters remain limited, constraining the development of microbial baselines for long-term monitoring. Surface seawater bacterial communities from four Korean coastal locations were analysed using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. Total bacterial...

item.title: Glycol chitosan thermogels: a versatile platform for advanced drug delivery
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Injectable thermogels are promising localized drug delivery platforms as their temperature-triggered in situ gelation facilitates practical administration. However, conventional systems suffer from high critical gelation concentrations, limited biodegradability, cytotoxicity, or acidic degradation, which can cause local inflammation. Glycol chitosan (GC)-based thermogels have emerged as a promising alternative, combining aqueous solubility at physiological pH, biodegradability,...

item.description: Klebsiella pneumoniae is a Gram-negative opportunistic pathogen responsible for severe healthcare-associated infections. In this study, we isolated Jasmi2, a lytic bacteriophage targeting K2-type K. pneumoniae strains. item.description: Lead (Pb) exposure during the perinatal period poses significant neurodevelopmental risks to the fetus and infant, yet no physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model has characterized the full maternal-placental-lactational Pb continuum for East Asian populations. item.title: Protein nanocages: Programmable biomaterial platforms for therapeutics, bioimaging, and diagnostics
item.description: Protein nanocages are monodisperse, hollow structures formed through the symmetric self-assembly of protein subunits. Their genetically encoded architectures combine the geometric precision of nanoscale assemblies with the intrinsic biocompatibility and functional versatility of naturally evolved proteins. item.description: BACKGROUND: Gallbladder and biliary diseases-including cholelithiasis, cholecystitis, cholangitis, and other non-malignant biliary tract disorders-are important contributors to the global digestive disease burden, but a global, comprehensive, and systematic estimation of their burden is absent. We aimed to quantify long-term trends and current patterns in prevalence, mortality, and disability associated with gallbladder and biliary diseases across geographies, sexes, and ages.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The cost-effectiveness of uniform biennial endoscopic screening in Korea declined substantially between 2012 and 2022 and the 2022 results were markedly less favourable for women than for men. These findings support periodic reassessment of mature screening programmes and further evaluation of differentiated screening approaches.

item.title: Viral potential to modulate antibiotic resistance gene succession through host interactions during food waste composting
item.description: Composting can mitigate antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) risks, yet viral contributions to their dynamics remain unclear. Using time-series metagenomics, we investigated viral roles in ARG succession during composting of two food waste types. In both composts, ARGs followed an enrichment-decline-rebound trajectory accompanied by substrate-specific ARG-host turnover. item.description: CONCLUSION: Factors influencing eHbA1c-mHbA1c concordance differ by CGM duration. While 14-day data require higher AT (≥78%) for accuracy, 90-day data provide more stable estimates. Clinical interpretation must account for mHbA1c, TIR, and sensor type, especially when using shorter-term CGM profiles in Asian individuals with T1DM.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Measuring the solid component narrows but does not close the difference in pathologic risk between part-solid and solid adenocarcinoma of the same size. These associations warrant external validation and evaluation in preoperative risk models.

In this study, we developed benzo[d]oxazole-based NAMPT inhibitors through structure-guided optimization from SW008135, involving sequential modifications of the distal substituent, linker architecture, and benzo[d]oxazole scaffold. item.title: Spousal caregiving and depressive symptoms among middle-aged and older adults in Korea: The role of the family effect
item.description: Recent evidence suggests that commonly reported caregiving-depression associations may partly reflect a methodological artifact - omission of the "family effect," the direct psychological toll of a loved one's functional decline, which simultaneously precipitates caregiving and independently elevates depressive symptoms. item.title: Elimination kinetics of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs during carbon hemoperfusion in 19 dogs with toxicosis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Carbon hemoperfusion was associated with substantial reductions in plasma NSAID concentrations during treatment in dogs with severe ibuprofen, carprofen, or naproxen toxicosis. Most of the decline occurred early in the session. Further studies are warranted to optimize treatment protocols.

item.title: Integrated genomic and transcriptomic profiling identifies PFKM as a candidate biomarker of nodal metastasis in oral squamous cell carcinoma
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This integrated analysis identifies PFKM as a stable biomarker candidate associated with nodal metastasis in OSCC and highlights the coordinated involvement of metabolic and Wnt/β-catenin-related pathways in metastatic progression.

item.title: Development and Content Validation of a Self-Assessment Checklist for Electronic Medical Record Use Certification in Korea: Convergent Mixed Methods Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The self-assessment checklist demonstrated high content validity and was perceived as relevant for evaluating patient safety-critical aspects of EMR use. However, expert-assessed feasibility varied across health care institution types, particularly in clinic-level settings. Further empirical testing is needed to assess the checklist's reliability, usability, and applicability in real-world certification processes.

item.description: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder primarily characterized by motor impairments and altered whole-body coordination. item.description: HLA-E is a non-classical MHC class I molecule with restricted polymorphism, offering a putative path to broadly applicable off-the-shelf therapies. item.title: Oocyte yield according to initiation timing in random-start controlled ovarian hyperstimulation
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The menstrual cycle phase at stimulation initiation influences ovarian response during random-start COH. The LL phase represents an effective window for stimulation initiation, and luteal phase initiation is particularly advantageous for maximizing oocyte yield in patients with low ovarian reserve who require urgent FP.

item.title: Validation study of the Korean version of the parent protection scale
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study provides evidence that the Korean PPS is a culturally adapted tool with acceptable overall reliability for assessing parental protection, with the potential to inform family-centered care and culturally adapted interventions. In clinical practice, it may support more precise identification of protective parenting patterns and guide targeted interventions to balance protection with the promotion of child autonomy.

item.title: From trial efficacy to real-world effectiveness: evaluating the generalizability of cisplatin-gemcitabine-durvalumab in advanced biliary tract cancers
item.description: CONCLUSION: The survival outcomes observed in the TOPAZ-1 CGD arm were broadly reproduced in this large real-world cohort. Findings for ECOG PS 0 and locally advanced disease are exploratory and should be interpreted cautiously because of reduced effective sample size and limited empirical overlap.

item.title: Clinicopathological differences between asymptomatic vs symptomatic breast cancer: a 30-year single-center retrospective study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Symptomatic breast cancer represents a clinically distinct presentation associated with adverse clinicopathologic features and persistently poorer long-term outcomes, even after adjustment for established prognostic factors. Despite the benefits of screening, the persistent burden of symptomatic disease underscores the need for public health strategies focused on early symptom awareness and regular breast self-examination.

item.title: Cumulative sport-related concussions alter cortical responses to acute aerobic exercise in rugby players
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Acute aerobic exercise was associated with improved cognition and modulation of resting-state EEG activity, while cumulative SRC exposure impaired exercise-induced cortical responsivity, particularly in EO occipital gamma responses.

item.title: Effects of acute resistance exercise intensity on asprosin, glycemic markers and appetite responses in obese and non-obese women
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Acute high-intensity resistance exercise effectively reduces asprosin concentrations and improves glycemic control in women with obesity; however, these metabolic benefits may be offset by compensatory increases in hunger and energy intake. These findings suggest that exercise prescriptions for women with obesity should incorporate concurrent dietary strategies to prevent postexercise compensatory eating from negating the metabolic advantages of high-intensity resistance exercise.

item.title: Urea oxidation reaction for energy-efficient hydrogen production: mechanisms, catalysts, and electrolysis systems
item.description: Urea oxidation offers an attractive pathway toward energy-efficient hydrogen production and simultaneous wastewater treatment. This review examines reaction mechanisms, dynamic catalyst reconstruction, and electrocatalyst design strategies, and critically evaluates their implications for electrolyzer performance, highlighting reaction selectivity, catalyst durability, mass transport, and realistic feed conditions as key challenges toward practical implementation.

item.description: In many languages, the pitch contour at the end of a sentence signals whether a speaker is asserting, asking, or conveying an attitude such as regret or admiration. item.description: CONCLUSION: A single booster dose of LEM-mR203 was well tolerated, with no major safety concerns over 366 days, and with exploratory cellular responses suggesting an IFN-γ-oriented profile without Th2 skewing. item.description: Herpesviruses establish lifelong latency and can reactivate when antiviral immune surveillance is compromised. item.description: Patient-specific quality assurance (PSQA) based on electronic portal imaging devices (EPIDs) is widely used for pretreatment verification, but it is usually performed as a single check of the approved plan and reflects the daily state of the linac only to a limited extent. item.description: Next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based measurable residual disease (MRD) detection in AML may be limited by non-leukemic hematopoietic cells in bulk bone marrow samples. To address this limitation, we aimed to evaluate whether CD34-positive cell enrichment improves the detectability of residual variants. Paired MRD analyses were performed using unsorted and CD34-enriched bone marrow samples from patients with CD34-positive AML, tracking leukemia-associated variants identified at diagnosis in...

item.title: History and Future of Efficient Design of Quality Control in Clinical Laboratories
item.description: After half a century of development, conventional quality control (QC) theory has begun to approach its practical limits. Classical theories, including power function analysis, multi-rules, and patient risk models, have pushed conventional QC to its near-maximal efficiency. This review discusses this historical development and explores how patient-based real-time QC (PBRTQC) can theoretically drive future improvements in the information age. We focus on the key, yet often overlooked, concept of...

item.title: Commentary: Surgical Correction of Mitral Paravalvular Leak: Safer Operations, Unresolved Durability

item.description: No abstract

item.title: Three-Year Real-World Outcomes of Switching to Brolucizumab for Refractory Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Switching to brolucizumab provided maintained visual and anatomical improvements with extended treatment intervals over 3 years. The safety profile was consistent with previous reports, and IOI events were manageable in a real-world setting.

item.title: Loss of the Steep-Axis Flattening Effect in Sutured Clear Corneal Incisions: A Single-Surgeon Vector Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this single-surgeon series of sutured clear corneal incisions, steep-axis incisions did not produce the expected flattening of the incision meridian, and the SIA acted predominantly as torque with a mean steepening effect. Whether the routine suture contributes to this pattern remains to be confirmed by direct sutured-versus-sutureless comparison.

item.title: The Reporting-Service Gap in Intimate Partner Violence: Police Reporting, Victim-Service Receipt, and Dual Noncontact in the National Crime Victimization Survey, 1993-2023
item.description: Research on intimate partner violence (IPV) underreporting often treats police notification as the primary indicator of formal-system reach, leaving less clear whether incidents not reported to police include recorded receipt of help or advice from victim-service agencies. Using incident-level public-use data from the National Crime Victimization Survey (NCVS), 1993 to 2023, this study examines the joint distribution of police reporting and receipt of victim-service help or advice among IPV...

item.title: Development and Psychometric Validation of the Korean Version of the Velopharyngeal Insufficiency Effects on Life Outcomes
item.description: ObjectiveTo develop and validate a culturally adapted Korean version of the Velopharyngeal Insufficiency Effects on Life Outcomes (K-VELO) for children with cleft palate with or without cleft lip (CP ± L).DesignMethodological study including linguistic validation and psychometric evaluation.Setting: Tertiary cleft centers in South Korea.Participants: A total of 74 children and 78 parents completed the K-VELO; 72 children and 62 parents also completed perceptual speech evaluations. For...

item.title: Assessment of health and nutrition issues and strategic directions for tailored nutrition management in a rural area of Gangwon State, Korea: a mixed-methods study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Health and nutrition problems in this rural setting may reflect individual behaviors and structural and environmental constraints. Preventive, family-based strategies targeting young and middle-aged adults are warranted. Tailored interventions integrating dietary improvement, physical activity, and local context are needed to reduce health disparities and improve community health.

item.title: An exploration of the participation experiences of university students in a social cognitive theory-based digital health behavior intervention program in Korea: a qualitative study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Pairing mobile self-monitoring with online community interaction provides valuable qualitative insights into how students experience health behavior engagement. Peer facilitation shapes a distinct contextual environment which influences user motivation, peer interaction, and social support perception. These findings offer foundational qualitative perspectives to aid in the design of potential health promotion strategies on university campuses.

item.title: Comparison of health, functional, and dietary characteristics between low-income and general income community-dwelling older adults in Korea: a cross-sectional study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Low-income older adults were more likely to have poor health status, functional limitations, oral health problems, and insufficient intake of several food groups than general income older adults. Therefore, effective interventions to improve the dietary quality of community-dwelling older adults must go beyond simple food provision and adopt an integrated approach that incorporates tailored functional support, oral health management, and sex-specific nutrition education.

item.title: Changes in hygiene management performance across monitoring visit rounds in long-term care institutions for older adults in Korea: a retrospective longitudinal observational study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Repeated hygiene and safety monitoring visits were associated with improved hygiene management performance in long-term care institutions for older adults, particularly during the early stages of repeated visits. Such field-based guidance and feedback may contribute to the strengthening of hygiene management practices in small-scale institutions.

item.title: Embedding person-centered nutrition assessment and care in Korea's Community Integrated Care for older adults and persons with disabilities: 'From Policy to Fork': a narrative review
item.description: CONCLUSION: Nutrition could function as a core operational domain of community integrated care rather than solely as nutrition education or meal delivery. Existing dietitian-led foodservice infrastructure and standard nutrition-management algorithms provide a foundation, but field-validated assessment modules, explicit accountability, service maps, and human-governed digital tools may need to be developed and evaluated. The proposed 'From Policy to Fork' framework is offered as a conceptual...

item.title: Longitudinal Mean HbA1c and Electrodiagnostic Severity of Distal Symmetric Sensorimotor Polyneuropathy in Type 2 Diabetes: Comparison With Index HbA1c
item.description: CONCLUSION: Mean HbA1c showed more consistent associations than index HbA1c across separate models, but superiority was not established. Sensitivity analyses indicated uncertainty in the ordinal association.

item.title: Energy-band alignment of stacked single-crystalline Si/α-Ga2O3p-n heterojunctions
item.description: A stacked single-crystalline Si/α-Ga(2)O(3)p-n heterojunction was formed by transferring a 100 nm p-Si nanomembrane onto anα-Ga(2)O(3)epiwafer. Theα-Ga(2)O(3)layer exhibited a (110) x-ray diffraction reflection, and the epi-layer at the Si/α-Ga(2)O(3)interface had a valence-band maximum located 4.29 ± 0.10 eV below the Fermi-level. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy depth profiling revealed decreases of 0.11 eV in the Si 2p binding energy and 0.35 eV in the Ga 3d binding energy from the bulk-like...

item.title: Multiscale Freestanding Vertically Aligned CNT Heat Sink Enabling Multimodal Heat Dissipation by Conduction, Convection, and Radiation
item.description: A vertically aligned carbon nanotube (VACNT)-based heat sink is demonstrated for passive multimodal thermal management applicable for electronic and semiconductor devices. The VACNT enables multimodal heat dissipation through axial conduction, convection facilitated by its nanoporous morphology, and radiation enabled by its superior emissivity. While conventional metallic heat sinks suffer from low surface emissivity and require complex post-processing to enhance radiative cooling, the proposed...

item.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and the Eye: Ocular Safety, Retinal Outcomes, and Clinical Implications
item.description: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists have transformed the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, but rapidly expanding use has generated concern about ocular adverse events. In Korea, newly established national health insurance reimbursement criteria for injectable semaglutide (Ozempic prefilled pen) took effect on February 1, 2026; as use among eligible patients may expand, proportionate ophthalmic preparedness is timely. This structured narrative review evaluates randomized trials,...

item.title: Global Trends and Burden of HIV Coinfection With Extensively Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis From 1990 to 2021: The Global Burden of Disease Study 2021
item.description: CONCLUSION: Despite declines in HIV/XDR-TB burden, significant regional and demographic disparities persist, highlighting the need for targeted public health strategies in high-burden regions.

item.title: Impact of Neuromuscular Blocking Agents on Hospital Outcomes in Mechanically Ventilated Patients With Sepsis: Propensity Score Analyses of A Nationwide Sepsis Cohort
item.description: CONCLUSION: In patients with sepsis requiring MV, the use of NMBAs was not associated with in-hospital mortality but was linked to longer ICU stays and a higher incidence of ventilator-associated pneumonia. These findings underscore the need for cautious use of continuous NMBA infusion in this population.

item.title: Impact of Mass Resignation of Junior Doctors in Korea on Major Interventions: Interrupted Time Series Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: The mass resignation of junior doctors was associated with substantial and immediate reductions in healthcare service provision across multiple clinical specialties, particularly in tertiary hospitals. The absence of immediate effects for certain DPNIs likely reflects their lower reliance on junior doctors, as well as the urgency or structural characteristics of these interventions. These findings highlight the need for health policies that address unmet healthcare needs and mitigate...

item.title: Lifetime Endogenous Estrogen Exposure Predicts Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis Risk in Postmenopausal Women Based on a Nationwide Population Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Among postmenopausal women, lifetime endogenous estrogen exposure showed a protective role from developing IPF.

item.title: Circulating Estradiol as an Independent Risk Factor for Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Fibrosis Risk in Women: Evidence From a Multicenter Health-Checkup Cohort
item.description: CONCLUSION: Low circulating estradiol independently increases the risk of MASLD and high-risk fibrosis in women. While its protective effect against steatosis weakens with obesity, its antifibrotic effect remains strong across all subgroups. Estradiol may serve as an important hormonal marker for risk stratification in female MASLD patients.

item.title: Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve Shaving With a Blade During Transoral Robotic Thyroidectomy
item.description: This video demonstrates blade-based recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) shaving during transoral robotic thyroidectomy in four patients with papillary thyroid carcinoma and tumor adherence to a functioning RLN. Controlled sharp dissection along the tumor-nerve interface enabled anatomical nerve preservation in all four cases, with normal vocal fold mobility at 3 months.

item.title: Association between seafood consumption and urinary bisphenol concentrations in Korean adults: findings from the Korean National Environmental Health Survey (KoNEHS 2018-2020)
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Seafood-frequency categories showed associations with spot urinary concentrations of BPA, BPF, and BPS. These cross-sectional findings do not establish a causal relationship or a specific exposure pathway. Longitudinal studies with repeated urinary measurements and more detailed assessment of seafood products, processing, and food-contact materials are needed to clarify these associations.

item.title: Machine Learning-Based Risk Scoring Using Clinical and Surgical Variables for Severe Complications after Rectal Cancer Surgery
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Machine learning-based models accurately predicted severe postoperative complications after rectal cancer surgery, with strong discrimination maintained on temporal internal validation. Applied immediately after surgery, they may support individualized postoperative risk stratification and monitoring; external validation is warranted. See Video Abstract.

item.title: Lost, then found: transient forgetting in humans and machines
item.description: Forgetting can be permanent or transient. An intriguing, recently described form of transient forgetting (TF) in artificial neural networks is the stability gap: a network that has already learned a first task exhibits transient yet substantial forgetting when it begins additional training on a second task alongside the first. Could an analogous phenomenon be found in humans? Following a literature survey, six types of TF in humans were identified, categorised by their sources: learning,...

item.title: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay-based screening approach for phage-independent affinity maturation of single-domain antibodies
item.description: Because of its high specificity and stability, the single variable domain of the heavy chain of a heavy-chain camel antibody (VHH) is an essential component in diagnostics and therapeutics. However, VHHs derived from immune or synthetic libraries often require affinity maturation to meet clinical or industry requirements. Although phage display has been widely used for this purpose, it is prone to selection bias and requires re-cloning steps. Here, we developed a phage-independent screening...

item.title: Factors Associated with Perceived Voice Age in Community-Dwelling Older Adults in Japan: A Cross-Sectional Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Perceived voice age partially reflects chronological age. Higher grip strength, better hearing ability, and higher cognitive performance were associated with younger perceived voice age in women. Although interpretation in men is limited by sample characteristics, these findings suggest that perceived voice age may reflect multiple physiological and cognitive domains.

item.title: Beyond sequence: a half-life × localization framework for lncRNAs
item.description: Why do long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) with similar sequences behave differently across cell types and stimuli? This opinion article argues that reading half-life together with subcellular localization provides a practical organizing dimension for lncRNA function, one that helps make sense of the context-dependent, stimulus-responsive, and tissue-specific behaviors that sequence and structure alone leave unexplained. Drawing on transcriptome-wide turnover data from RNA sequencing and related...

item.title: Risk of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism after simultaneous bilateral knee arthroplasty: A Japanese nationwide medical claims database study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Simultaneous bilateral knee arthroplasty is associated with an increased risk of postoperative deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, despite routine postoperative antithrombotic medications. Careful perioperative management is therefore essential when considering simultaneous bilateral procedures, particularly with regard to thromboembolic risk.

item.title: Treatment strategies for obliterative bronchiolitis associated with connective tissue diseases: a scoping review
item.description: Obliterative bronchiolitis associated with connective tissue diseases (OB-CTD) is a severe and progressive pulmonary condition. Characterised by inflammation and fibrosis of the small airways, it leads to significant morbidity. Despite its severity, OB-CTD often remains underdiagnosed and the lack of standardised, evidence-based treatment guidelines poses a substantial clinical challenge. This scoping review consolidates current knowledge of the treatment of OB-CTD. The review aims to raise...

item.title: Influence of conversion factors on 24-h urine-derived estimates compared with self-reported protein, sodium, or potassium intake in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: Accurate dietary assessment is essential for quantifying absolute nutrient intake and diet-disease relationships. However, self-reports often lack precision, and their validity is commonly evaluated against recovery biomarkers derived from 24-h urinary collection (UC). However, biomarker-based intake estimates depend on the applied urinary conversion factors, which may influence conclusions about misreporting. We aimed to quantify the mean differences in protein, sodium, or potassium intake...

item.title: Spatial architecture of the synovium identifies clinically relevant phenotypes of osteoarthritis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate that the spatial organization of synovial architecture, beyond simple tissue composition, captures clinically relevant heterogeneity in knee OA and links histological microenvironments to cell-cell communication networks.

item.title: Peritonsillar abscess and Lemierre syndrome: sequential progression or overlapping pathways in Fusobacterium necrophorum infection?
item.description: The relationship between peritonsillar abscess (PTA) and Lemierre syndrome (LS) in Fusobacterium necrophorum infection remains incompletely understood. This hypothesis-generating narrative mini-review examines how clinically recognized PTA and LS may be related. Contemporary PTA cohorts report few or no recognized LS or septic thrombophlebitis events during follow-up, whereas LS-based series show substantial variation in the frequency of documented PTA. item.title: Dual limit determination for recirculation control against inhibition and sludge washout in anammox expanded granular sludge bed reactor
item.description: Recirculation simultaneously alleviates substrate inhibition through dilution and intensifies sludge washout through increased upflow velocity, yet these opposing effects are rarely quantified as explicit limits for recirculation control. A dual limit approach was established for an anammox expanded granular sludge bed (EGSB) reactor treating partial-nitrification-pretreated food-waste anaerobic digestion dewatering liquor, with lower and upper recirculation limits defined by inhibition control...

item.title: Immunogenicity and Safety of Maternal DTaP Vaccination: The OKINAWA Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Maternal DTaP vaccination increased antibody levels responses without identified safety concerns, supporting its potential role in preventing infant pertussis.

item.title: Low Cross-Sectional Area of the Geniohyoid muscle Is Associated With Non-Home Discharge in Older Patients Admitted to the Emergency Department
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Low GH-CSA at admission was independently associated with non-home discharge among older patients hospitalized in an acute care setting. Ultrasound assessment of GH-CSA may serve as a simple and objective marker for early identification of patients at high risk of adverse discharge outcomes.

item.title: Phenotypic and Genomic Characterization of Five Novel Klebsiella Bacteriophages: Exploring the Relationship Between Spot-Lysis Patterns and Host Defense Systems
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Spot-lysis patterns were not readily explained by the bacterial characteristics examined or by any single defense system, suggesting that additional host and phage factors may contribute. ΦKpT256 and the three Siphovirus-like phages showed differing species-level spot-lysis profiles and warrant evaluation as potential components of a KpSC-targeted phage cocktail.

item.description: Considerable data support the hypothesis that hypoxia plays a central role in the development of atherosclerotic plaques and cardiovascular disease. item.title: First epidemiological and molecular characterization of bovine leukemia virus in Holstein dairy cattle from two cities in Shandong Province, China
item.description: Bovine leukemia virus (BLV) is the etiological origin of enzootic bovine leukosis, a chronic lymphoproliferative disorder causing significant economic losses to the global cattle industry. Shandong Province in eastern China is a major dairy cattle-breeding region. However, the molecular prevalence and genetic characteristics of BLV in this area remain unclear. In this study, 289 blood samples were collected from Holstein dairy cattle across three large-scale commercial farms in Shandong...

item.title: Zooming in on anti-Zo-positive antisynthetase syndrome: A multicenter case series and literature review
item.description: CONCLUSION: IP-MS is a reliable detection method for anti-Zo autoantibodies. Anti-Zo-positive ASyS is characterized by typical ASyS features, but in some patients SSc-like features can be present.

item.title: Best practices in communication of environmental health risks due to localised pollution events: a mixed-methods systematic review
item.description: Localised environmental pollution can generate acute concern, particularly when the health effects are uncertain. Media coverage can amplify fear and stress, necessitating transparent risk communication. This mixed-methods systematic Review (PROSPERO registration number CRD42024568007) focuses on strategies for communicating health risks associated with local pollution. We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, Scopus, and PsycArticles on April 19, 2024, (from inception) and May 22, 2026 (Jan 1,...

item.title: Breathlessness mechanisms, measurement, and management in adults: evidence update on behalf of The Dyspnoea Society
item.description: Breathlessness affects an estimated 40% of adults living with chronic disease, with substantial consequences for individuals, carers, and health-care systems. This Dyspnoea Society Research Statement, developed for researchers, clinicians, and adults living with or caring for someone with breathlessness, provides a state-of-the-art synthesis of recent advances in chronic breathlessness mechanisms, measurement, and management, and outlines a research agenda for the next decade. Key advancements...

item.title: Intermittent fasting enhances muscle regeneration via an EDA2R-NIK-myomixer axis
item.description: Skeletal muscle exhibits a remarkable regenerative capacity that relies on adult stem cells known as satellite cells (SCs), which differentiate into myogenic progenitors to drive muscle repair. How varying energy availability alters myogenesis, however, remains unknown. Here, we demonstrate that intermittent fasting (IF) in mice upregulates a myogenic gene program, including Myomixer, a muscle-specific fusogen that facilitates the merging of progenitor cells into myofibers. IF enhances the...

item.title: Distinct age-related associations of equol production status with cardiometabolic, oxidative stress and bone biomarkers in Japanese women
item.description: CONCLUSION: Approximately 29% of the study participants were equol producers, but their equol production might not be consistent. Equol producer status might be associated with multiple health benefits, but these might depend on the life stage of the individual.

item.title: Defining mental health physiotherapy: An international qualitative study of experts in mental health physiotherapy
item.description: CONCLUSION: Findings indicate that mental health physiotherapy reflects a philosophical shift towards the explicit integration of mind and body, rather than a discrete area defined by clinical setting, population, or intervention. Based on these findings, a new definition of mental health physiotherapy is proposed. CONTRIBUTION OF THE PAPER.

item.title: Evaluation of image-matching and prostate movement angle using anatomical characteristics obtained from planning computed tomography
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Image-matching and prostate movement angles differed between groups stratified according to patient anatomical characteristics, suggesting the potential utility of anisotropic margins and careful patient setup.

item.title: Gender equity in the global rheumatology workforce: results of the Coalition for Health and Gender Equity (CHANGE) survey
item.description: CONCLUSION: This global survey provides compelling evidence of gender disparities in rheumatology, necessitating coordinated, evidence-based interventions to address structural barriers and promote inclusive cultures.

item.title: Oxygen fugacity, temperature, and pressure of Siberian eclogitic diamonds: Implications for the Archaean convecting mantle redox state
item.description: Kimberlite-borne eclogite xenoliths ultimately derive from ancient subducted oceanic crust. Some specimens still record the chemical and redox conditions of their igneous protoliths, allowing a view into contemporaneous convecting mantle sources. However, accurate reconstructions are limited because eclogites have been exposed to metasomatism in the subcontinental mantle for billions of years. Here, we investigated garnet and clinopyroxene inclusions, both touching and nontouching pairs, in 19...

item.title: Common transcriptional changes in the brain during hibernation and Alzheimer's disease
item.description: Hibernation demands rapid brain adaptations, involving cycles of reduced metabolic rate during torpor, followed by brief periods of arousal. Previous studies show hibernation induces a drastic increase in Tau hyperphosphorylation, but a mechanistic connection to disease remains unclear. Using single-nucleus RNA sequencing on hippocampi of golden hamsters, we unveil large transcriptional shifts across the hibernation cycle in all cell types, especially glia. Common transcriptional changes in...

item.title: The YAP/TAZ-Tgfbr2-stiffness feedback loop governs divergent cell fates of muscle-resident mesenchymal progenitors
item.description: Mesenchymal progenitors are essential for muscle regeneration, but also contribute to fat accumulation and fibrosis. Several extrinsic and intrinsic factors regulating adipogenic or fibrogenic differentiation of mesenchymal progenitors have been identified. However, it remains unclear how different cues are integrated to determine cell fate. Here, we demonstrate that interstitial stiffness and the mechanosensitive hippo pathway regulate mesenchymal progenitor cell fate. Fat accumulation model...

item.title: Damage Assessment of Major Soybean Viruses in Korea: Infection Timing Influences Yield Loss and Seed-Borne Transmission Dynamics
item.description: Soybean mosaic virus (SMV; species Potyvirus glycitessellati) and soybean yellow mottle mosaic virus (SYMMV; species Gammacarmovirus glycinis) are predominant viral pathogens threatening soybean production. While their high prevalence during early vegetative stages has been increasingly reported, the quantitative epidemiological impact of infection timing on ultimate crop yield and seed-borne transmission dynamics remains poorly understood. In this study, we evaluated the effect of SMV and SYMMV...

item.title: Insomnia partially mediates the association between ADHD traits and depressive symptoms in Japanese nursing students
item.description: Nursing students with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) traits may struggle with demanding academic and clinical training, potentially increasing the risk of insomnia and depressive symptoms. This study examined whether insomnia statistically mediates the association between ADHD traits and depressive symptoms in this population. item.title: Resection for Recurrent Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: Preoperative CA19-9 and Host Immunonutritional Status Stratify Overall Survival
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Increased tumor marker burden and impaired immunonutritional status were associated with poor survival after resection for recurrent PDAC. Integrating tumor biology and host condition into preoperative assessments may inform multidisciplinary surgical decision-making and help prevent futile resection.

item.title: Identification of risk factors underlying a decline in gait speed in older individuals
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: We developed a simple scoring system to predict gait speed decline in older adults. Currently, it should be considered an exploratory risk stratification tool; external validation may support its future clinical use.

item.title: TREM2-LRP1 axis in Alzheimer's disease: pharmacological trade-offs of receptor shedding and functional restoration
item.description: The interplay between triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) and low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1 (LRP1) is critical for amyloid-beta (Aβ) clearance in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Current therapeutic strategies targeting this axis can be broadly divided into two pharmacological approaches: indirect induction via metabolic modulation (e.g., ACAT1 inhibition) and direct functional restoration of LRP1. While ACAT1 inhibition effectively upregulates LRP1, recent...

item.title: Virtual Flood Experience Enhances Preparedness Through Emotional and Neural Engagement
item.description: As climate change intensifies flood risks, strengthening individual preparedness is essential for sustainable societies. This study tested whether first-person three-dimensional computer graphics (3DCG) flood videos can complement official flood maps in motivating preparedness. We used these materials as operationalizations of experiential and descriptive information, respectively. In a preregistered web experiment with 1000 participants, those who viewed flood videos showed a small but...

item.title: Prevalence and prognostic implications of systemic autoinflammatory and autoimmune diseases in myelodysplastic neoplasms: a retrospective Belgian cohort study
item.description: Myelodysplastic neoplasms (MDS) are clonal hematopoietic disorders marked by ineffective hematopoiesis and an increased risk of progression to acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Growing evidence highlights the role of inflammation in MDS pathogenesis, and systemic autoinflammatory and autoimmune diseases (SIAD) are increasingly recognized as comorbidities. However, data regarding their prognostic implications are conflicting. In this retrospective study, we evaluated 163 patients diagnosed with MDS...

item.title: Anterior Capsulorhexis Optic Capture for Zonular Insufficiency: Three-Year Outcomes With a Retinitis Pigmentosa Subanalysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: ACOC was associated with stable visual, refractive, and anatomical outcomes for up to 3 years in eyes with maintained optic capture. In high-risk RP eyes, progressive capsulorhexis contraction was not observed beyond 3 months.

item.title: Understanding Cultural Variations in Stigma Related to Hearing Health
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Ethnicity and generational status were key predictors of public and self-stigma, highlighting the role of sociocultural context in shaping perceptions of HL and hearing aid use. This suggests that a uniform approach to addressing stigma may be inadequate, as experiences of stigma may differ across cultural and generational contexts. Future qualitative work is needed to better understand lived experiences of stigma within and between ethnic groups to ground the development of...

item.title: Electron-Beam-Assisted Formation of Simple-Cubic Silver
item.description: Accessing crystal phases under nonequilibrium conditions is a central challenge for expanding the landscape of materials. Simple-cubic (sc) structures are considered energetically unfavorable in elemental solids and have previously been confirmed only in polonium. Here, we report the direct observation of a previously unrecognized sc-Ag formed under far-from-equilibrium conditions. Using electron beam irradiation inside a high-resolution transmission electron microscope as a trigger, we induced...

item.title: Cathodoluminescence Wavefront Retrieval
item.description: Free-electron-based nanoscopy enables the study of optical excitations in materials with deep-subwavelength spatial resolution, with cathodoluminescence (CL) being one of the most useful signals. When combined with an optical collection system, CL measurements can access multidimensional information on light; yet the phase of the emitted optical fields has remained largely elusive. item.description: CONCLUSION: TCA shows a high prevalence of genetic abnormalities and substantial postoperative and long-term morbidity, independent of surgical technique.

item.description: Edentulism can lead to psychological occlusal fatigue, dysphonia, facial deformity, and reduced quality of life. item.title: Fully deuterated [9]cycloparaphenylene: vibrational modulation for enhanced solid-state fluorescence
item.description: Fully deuterated [9]cycloparaphenylene ([9]CPP-d(36)) was synthesized by gold-mediated macrocyclization. Although the molecular geometry and π-electronic structure of [9]CPP were retained, the framework vibrational frequencies were lowered. Solid-state [9]CPP-d(36) showed a higher fluorescence quantum yield than [9]CPP (0.37 vs. 0.24), demonstrating H/D substitution as a vibrational-modulation approach for enhancing nanohoop fluorescence.

item.title: Hemodialysis access dysfunction caused by heavily calcified subclavian artery chronic total occlusion: Two cases treated with balloon-expandable covered stents
item.description: Proximal arterial inflow lesions are an underrecognized cause of hemodialysis access dysfunction, particularly in patients with advanced arterial calcification. item.title: Locus coeruleus microstructural integrity and sleep disruption in the context of Alzheimer's disease pathology
item.description: INTRODUCTION: The locus coeruleus (LC) is among the first sites of tau pathology in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and plays a key role in sleep-wake regulation. However, evidence linking LC integrity to objective sleep measures in the context of emerging AD pathology remains limited.
